title: Windows — Windshield Damage, Heating and the Delamination Dispatch Limitation

issue.reason: Original issue of the windshield damage, heating and delamination limitation entry.

abstract: Limitation entry covering windshield heating, the maximum speed with a damaged pane and the dispatch position when delamination is visible at the lower forward corner of a windshield.

sections.purpose: To state the windshield heating requirement, the speed limitation with a damaged pane and the dispatch position for visible delamination.
sections.description: The windshield is a laminated structural pane and its heating is not only for demisting; the heat keeps the outer ply at a temperature at which it retains its impact resistance. Operation without heating on a pane therefore carries a speed limitation, not merely a visibility one. Delamination appears as a milky or bubbled patch, usually starting at the lower forward corner where the heater terminal sits, and it grows slowly over weeks rather than suddenly. A small delaminated area away from the field of view is acceptable for dispatch under the conditions in the minimum equipment list; a delaminated area that has grown between two checks, or one that reaches the field of view, is not. An electrical smell in the flight compartment accompanied by any discolouration at a windshield corner is treated as a failed pane regardless of how small the affected area is, and the heating for that pane is selected off.
sections.crew_procedure: During the exterior check, look at the lower forward corner of each windshield and compare what you see with the record of the last report. During the cockpit preparation confirm both windshield heating systems operate. In flight, if an electrical smell is noticed together with discolouration at a windshield corner, select that pane's heating off, apply the speed limitation and land at a suitable airfield. Report any change in a delaminated area with a photograph where the operator's procedure allows it.
sections.limitation_note: With windshield heating inoperative on either pane, the maximum indicated airspeed below ten thousand feet is limited to 250 knots and flight into known or forecast icing is prohibited. A windshield with delamination that reaches the primary field of view, or that has measurably grown since the previous recorded inspection, is not acceptable for dispatch.

type_data.crew_action: Confirm both windshield heating systems operate; apply the speed limitation if either is inoperative.

title: Windows — Windshield Damage, Heating and the Delamination Dispatch Limitation

issue.reason: Applicability of the delamination limitation to both windshield standards confirmed and stated, with no change to the limits themselves.

abstract: Limitation entry covering windshield heating, the maximum speed with a damaged pane and the dispatch position when delamination is visible at the lower forward corner of a windshield.

sections.purpose: To state the windshield heating requirement, the speed limitation with a damaged pane and the dispatch position for visible delamination.
sections.description: The windshield is a laminated structural pane and its heating is not only for demisting; the heat keeps the outer ply at a temperature at which it retains its impact resistance. Operation without heating on a pane therefore carries a speed limitation, not merely a visibility one. Delamination appears as a milky or bubbled patch and grows slowly over weeks rather than suddenly. On the delivered standard it usually starts at the lower forward corner where the heater terminal sits; on the relocated terminal standard it more often starts along the lower edge. Either way a small delaminated area away from the field of view is acceptable for dispatch under the conditions in the minimum equipment list, and a delaminated area that has grown between two checks, or one that reaches the field of view, is not. An electrical smell in the flight compartment accompanied by any discolouration at a windshield corner is treated as a failed pane regardless of how small the affected area is, and the heating for that pane is selected off.
sections.crew_procedure: During the exterior check, look at the lower forward corner and along the lower edge of each windshield and compare what you see with the record of the last report. During the cockpit preparation confirm both windshield heating systems operate. In flight, if an electrical smell is noticed together with discolouration at a windshield corner, select that pane's heating off, apply the speed limitation and land at a suitable airfield. Report any change in a delaminated area with a photograph where the operator's procedure allows it.
sections.limitation_note: With windshield heating inoperative on either pane, the maximum indicated airspeed below ten thousand feet is limited to 250 knots and flight into known or forecast icing is prohibited. A windshield with delamination that reaches the primary field of view, or that has measurably grown since the previous recorded inspection, is not acceptable for dispatch. These limits apply to both windshield standards. The relocated heater terminal moves the place delamination usually starts but not what it means, and the acceptance criterion is the extent and the growth of the affected area rather than its position; the crew is not required to establish which standard the aircraft carries before applying this limitation. This was examined deliberately at the terminal relocation and the limits were left as they stand.

type_data.crew_action: Confirm both windshield heating systems operate; apply the speed limitation if either is inoperative.
